messages:
alex: quick follow-up from the autoscale RFC: proposing we split "admission" responsibilities out of the pool-operator. operator stays placement/leases/eviction; admission service handles cost/credits/fallback decisions. keeps operator simple and makes policy reusable across hosted/dedicated/private. comments?
maya: sounds good. what exactly does admission return? accept/reject only or richer hints?
alex: richer: decision + suggested fallback (model/quant/profile) + billing tag + expected cost/latency delta. operator still enforces hardware/region compatibility.
jong: main concerns: 1) added latency on hot path 2) race between admission decision and slot grant. we saw bad coupling cause an outage last quarter.
sophie: mitigations: short-lived caches (per-tenant) for low-latency lanes, optimistic admit window (n concurrent), and async path for batch lanes.
ralph: ledger question: admission needs credit state. central ledger = simpler correctness; local caches + periodic reconcile reduces latency but risks transient overspend. hybrid?
jong: hybrid seems pragmatic: central authoritative store, read replicas for admission, operator keeps tiny local reservoir for optimistic admits. reconciliation process to drain/charge properly.
infra-bot: note: admission-service v1 will be feature-flagged; read-replica support planned.
maya: compatibility: operator should send capability vector in admit call: {gpu_type, region, lane_class, seq_len_hint}. admission returns fallback only if compatible.
sophie: also return expected quality signal; admission returns {decision, fallback, cost_delta, latency_delta, quality_est}. operator can prefer latency or cost per route.
alex: example request/responses (pseudo):
POST /admit
{"tenant":"tn-42","req":{"model":"gptx-30b","gpu":"a100","lane":"low"},"context":{"burst_credits":2}}
response:
{"decision":"accept","fallback":{"model":"gptx-8b-q4"},"billing":"dedicated-tn42","cost_delta":-0.12,"latency_delta":+20}
jong: add trace_id/hash in response so operator+admission can reconcile. metrics: admit_latency, deny_reasons, optimistic_mismatch_count.
ralph: failure modes: 1) admission down -> operator uses local deterministic policy 2) ledger drift -> local reservoir + backpressure. we need audit logs for billing decisions.
maya: rollout plan: phase 0 advisory (admission suggests only), phase 1 gated enforcement for non-prod tenants, phase 2 enforced for all. collect suggested_vs_actual metrics.
sophie: cache TTLs: ~5s for low-latency, ~30s for batch; invalidate on top-up events. who owns TTL? operator decides per-lane.
alex: summary decisions: split admission from operator; hybrid ledger with central authority + local reservoir; optimistic window allowed with reconciliation; capability vector in API; phased rollout and strong telemetry/auth. please ack or object. :white_check_mark:
jong: ack, i'll open RFC PR with API schema and failure diagrams.
maya: ack, i'll own rollout metrics and gating rules.
ralph: ack, i'll design ledger auth and audit.
sophie: ack, i'll add cache heuristics and compatibility matrix to operator API.
infra-bot: created task INFRA-2176: "admission-controller prototype + operator integration" assigned to @jong.
